title: Interface Inheritance
concept: Interface inheritance (extends) lets one interface require another — building layered abstractions like Ord extends Eq.
why: Some interfaces naturally build on others: ordering requires equality, hashing requires equality. Inheritance expresses these dependencies cleanly.
tips: Use extends when one interface naturally requires another (Ord needs Eq)
extends reduces boilerplate — implementors don't need to list implied interfaces
A type implementing Ord automatically satisfies T: Eq bounds
Interface inheritance is about METHOD requirements, not data sharing
common_mistakes: Creating deep inheritance chains — 2-3 levels is usually enough
Confusing interface extends with implementation inheritance — interfaces define requirements, not behavior
Forgetting to implement parent interface methods — the compiler will remind you
